column1: # HOTD2 function prototypes and no-return flags — the committed source of truth
# for what the decompiler is told about a callee.
#   prototype   a C declaration, calling convention included:
#               `void __cdecl MatrixTranslate(float x, float y, float z)`.
#               Its name is for the reader; applying a row never renames.
#               `returns`      it does, and it has been wrongly flagged before;
#                              verify_ghidra_db fails if it is flagged again
#               `return@EDX:EAX`  custom storage for the return value
#              over MCP or in the GUI lands here)
# **Why this file exists.** 2,553 of the database's 2,735 functions had
# Ghidra's placeholder `undefined f()`, so the decompiler re-guessed every call
# site from the instructions around it. It gets integer pushes right and
# anything in an x87 register wrong: `__ftol` takes ST0, and 271 of its calls
# printed as `__ftol()` with the multiplier gone (L89). And the no-return
# flag is a claim about every caller at once -- two wrong ones cut 517
# functions short (L89). A row here is read by every call site, which
# is the point: fix the callee once instead of re-reading 700 callers.
# **Rows are sorted by address, and every writer keeps them that way.**
# Tags follow CLAUDE.md's evidence convention; a row without `[proved]` says why.

column4: Leaves its value on ST0 (FLD ST0 .. FSTP ST0 / RET); after two PUSHes it reads `curve` at [ESP+0xC] and `t` as FLD float ptr [ESP+0x10]. Without a float return every caller's use of it is a dropped ST0. [proved]

column2: void __cdecl CamEvalObjectPath6(int path, float t, void * out)
column4: out is {float x, y, z; int rx, ry, rz}: FSTP float ptr [EBP], [EBP+4], [EBP+8], then MOV dword ptr [EBP+0xC], [EBP+0x10], [EBP+0x14], EAX after each __ftol. Typed float * (as the decompiler guessed from the first three stores) the three rotations print as `(float)lVar3`, a conversion the code does not make (L89). void * lets each store carry its own type until the struct is declared. [proved]

Eight plain RETs, so it returns and the caller cleans up. The "Non-Returning Functions - Discovered" analyzer flagged it in the live database, which cut every hit arm the decompiler showed at its sound (L89). [proved]

The entry is PUSH ECX (a local) and PUSH EBP, then MOV EBP, dword ptr [ESP + 0xC]: the object is the first stack argument, and ECX is overwritten (MOV CX, word ptr [EBP+0x1312]) before it is read. Ghidra had guessed __thiscall with the local as `this`, which printed the draw loop's row counter as the parameter. [proved]

Sixteen instructions, two RETs: 0 if count would underflow, else pops count and returns 1. Once flagged no-return; the CALL_RETURN overrides that left on 587 call sites cut 383 functions short, silently, after the flag itself was cleared (L89). [proved]

column2: void __cdecl MatrixTranslate(float x, float y, float z)
column4: row3 += x*row0 + y*row1 + z*row2, reading x, y, z at [ESP+4], [ESP+8], [ESP+0xC]. Unprototyped, the decompiler printed the floats as hex integers. [proved]
Copies g_identity_matrix to the top. [proved]

MSVC's float-to-integer: FISTP qword of ST0 under a truncating control word, the result in EDX:EAX. It has no stack argument, so the decompiler dropped the value every caller converts and typed the result by whatever it was stored into (L89). [proved]
_longjmp: no RET. [proved]

__exit calls the CRT's exit worker with the quick-exit arguments (PUSH 0; PUSH 1), which ends the process; the RET after it is unreachable. Flagged by the "Known" analyzer at import. [likely] -- the worker is not read here.
